source:
I need this to be in 3d. Create a polished, high-quality Roblox asymmetric horror game inspired by the gameplay loop of survivor-versus-juggernaut games, but with an original implementation and a complete visual theme based entirely around Undertale and Deltarune. The game begins in a detailed central lobby where all players spawn after joining the server and after every completed round. The lobby should feel welcoming yet mysterious, featuring a blend of locations inspired by Hometown, Castle Town, Snowdin, Waterfall, and New Home, with glowing crystals, golden flowers, wooden pathways, cozy lighting, subtle magical effects, ambient music, benches, NPC decorations, and decorative references to the worlds of Undertale and Deltarune without copying existing maps exactly. A large countdown timer is displayed above the center of the lobby, automatically beginning a new round every 20 seconds once the previous round has ended, with all players remaining in the lobby until the countdown reaches zero. During this time, a random player is selected to become the Killer while every other player becomes a Survivor, with a small cinematic transition before teleporting everyone into the chosen map. The match lasts exactly 6 minutes unless the Killer eliminates every Survivor before time expires. At the start of each round, teleport all players into a large, highly detailed map inspired by Undertale and Deltarune that combines several iconic environments into one seamless playable location, including dark forests, Castle Town streets, Snowdin forests, Waterfall caverns with glowing blue water, the Ruins with purple brick architecture, abandoned laboratories, mysterious corridors, and hidden shortcuts connected naturally together. The map should feature multiple elevations, looping pathways, dead ends, open plazas, narrow hallways, underground passages, caves, bridges, decorative buildings, puzzles that act as obstacles rather than progression requirements, interactive environmental details, and plenty of hiding places while remaining balanced for both Survivors and the Killer. The atmosphere should constantly feel tense, using dynamic lighting, volumetric fog, flickering lights, magical particles, glowing plants, echoing ambience, and subtle environmental effects to create suspense without making visibility unfair. Survivors should play in third person and have the objective of surviving until the timer reaches zero by using teamwork, movement, map knowledge, and interactive objectives such as repairing magical generators, activating ancient rune pillars, restoring dark fountains, or completing other thematic objectives spread across the map to earn progression and small advantages. Survivors should not be overpowered and must rely on evasion, teamwork, and intelligent positioning rather than combat. The Killer should function as a powerful juggernaut with significantly increased movement speed, high durability, unique supernatural abilities, powerful attacks, and the ability to pressure multiple Survivors at once while still allowing skilled Survivors opportunities to escape through clever movement and map awareness. The Killer wins by eliminating every Survivor before the 6-minute timer ends, while the Survivors win if at least one Survivor remains alive when the timer expires. After the match ends, display a polished victory screen showing whether the Killer or Survivors won, award coins and experience based on performance, then automatically teleport every player back to the main lobby where another 20-second countdown immediately begins before the next round starts. The entire experience should feature smooth animations, polished UI, responsive controls, optimized scripting, atmospheric sound design, immersive environmental storytelling, clean transitions between gameplay phases, balanced mechanics, and a professional Roblox experience that feels complete, replayable, visually impressive, and faithful to the atmosphere and emotional tone associated with Undertale and Deltarune while remaining an original game experience.
Also create a polished, professional user interface for selecting and equipping characters. In the main lobby, include a clearly labeled **Survivors** button and **Killers** button that open separate selection menus. The UI should display all unlocked characters in a clean grid with large portraits, their name, rarity, difficulty, abilities, and a short description of their playstyle. Only one Survivor and one Killer can be equipped at a time, and the currently equipped character should be highlighted with an animated "Equipped" indicator. Add smooth menu transitions, hover animations, preview models that slowly rotate, and detailed character statistics such as Speed, Stamina, Detection, Power, and Difficulty. Include lock icons for characters that have not yet been unlocked and provide space for future Survivors and Killers to be added easily. For the initial release, include only one playable Survivor and one playable Killer. The Survivor should specialize in evasion, possessing above-average movement speed, quick acceleration, excellent stamina, and abilities focused on escaping danger, creating distance, and avoiding the Killer rather than fighting. Their gameplay should reward map knowledge, positioning, and precise movement. The Killer should be a powerful tracking-focused juggernaut capable of locating Survivors through unique tracking abilities, revealing their approximate locations for short periods, and applying constant pressure across the map. In addition to strong close-range attacks, the Killer should possess multiple ranged abilities themed around Undertale and Deltarune-inspired magical attacks, such as projectiles, energy blasts, or summoned hazards, giving Survivors opportunities to dodge while making the Killer feel powerful and threatening. Design both character selection menus and the in-game HUD with a clean, modern style inspired by Undertale and Deltarune aesthetics, featuring smooth animations, readable fonts, subtle pixel-inspired design elements, and consistent visual effects that match the rest of the game's atmosphere.

answers.ask: How many survivors per round? The map size for a 1v4 chase is very different from 1v12.
answers.answer: Use a 1v4 format: one Killer and up to four Survivors per round. This keeps the initial release balanced and the map focused around readable chases and teamwork.

answers.ask: You asked for dead ends, but a chase map with dead ends corners survivors unfairly - should they be short pockets off a loop, or true dead ends?
answers.answer: Use short pockets off looping routes rather than true dead ends, so they provide hiding spots and risky obstacle spaces without guaranteeing a Survivor is trapped.

scene_prompt: Create a polished 3D asymmetric-horror experience with an original, whimsical dark-fantasy visual register: a detailed central lobby that blends a cozy small-town area, castle-like streets, snowy woodland, glowing cavern elements, and warm golden-flower gardens. Arrange wooden paths, benches, decorative NPC figures, glowing crystals, magical effects, and cozy pools of light around a central gathering space. Build a separate large 1v4 chase map as one seamless, highly detailed location: dark forests transition into castle-town streets, snowy woods, blue-water caverns, purple-brick ruins, abandoned laboratories, and mysterious corridors. Connect these areas through multiple elevations, looping routes, plazas, narrow hallways, underground passages, caves, bridges, decorative buildings, hidden shortcuts, and short hiding pockets branching from loops rather than trapping dead ends. Scatter physical objective landmarks such as magical generators, ancient rune pillars, and dark fountain structures across the map, with obstacle-like puzzle elements and numerous hiding places. Use tense but readable lighting, volumetric fog, flickering lamps, glowing plants, magical particles, and environmental storytelling throughout.
blob:
### 1. Genre
The dominant genre is Survival, specifically asymmetric 1v4 chase horror: one Killer hunts up to four Survivors through a map built around evasion, hiding, and fair pursuit routes.

### 2. Shape and preset
Use `warren-looping`, matching the 1 vs All preset. The chase map is a connected web of loops across forest, streets, ruins, caverns, laboratories, and corridors; its apparent dead ends are only short hiding pockets that rejoin or sit immediately off a loop. Drop the preset’s escape exit because survival is timed rather than escape-based.

### 3. Config requirements
Use `cover-los` for lockers, ruined alcoves, dense vegetation, cave recesses, and short concealment pockets that break pursuit sightlines. Use `building-interior` for traversable laboratories, purple-brick ruins, corridor structures, and decorative town buildings linked to exterior routes. Use `water-body` for glowing blue cavern water. Use `npc-population` for decorative non-hostile town and lobby NPC figures. Use `terrain-relief` for readable hills, cave levels, bridges, and raised streets without confusing the chase routes.

### 4. Layout requirements
Use `spawn-protected`: place one screened Killer start at a remote edge of the chase network and four separated Survivor starts around the outer loop, each with an immediate safe route into the map. Use `npc-population` placement for decorative NPC figures in the lobby gathering space and non-blocking town-side alcoves. No enemy emitters or escape trigger are required.

### 5. Layout components
Build two separate maps: a welcoming central lobby and a large seamless chase map. The lobby centers on a countdown gathering plaza, with wooden paths branching through cozy town façades, castle-street fragments, snowy trees, crystal caves, and golden-flower gardens; include benches, glowing crystals, magical effects, decorative NPCs, and warm light pools. The chase map transitions through dark forest, castle-town streets, snowy woodland, blue-water caverns, purple-brick ruins, abandoned laboratories, and mysterious corridors. Connect plazas, narrow halls, underground passages, caves, bridges, and elevated paths with repeated loop-backs and hidden shortcuts. Distribute magical generators, rune pillars, dark fountains, and obstacle-puzzle landmarks across distinct route sectors. Frame the lobby as a compact inviting hub and the chase map as a broad, readable top-down network with tense fog and flickering light.

### 6. Render order
Use `topdown` first and make it authoritative, because invalid loop connectivity or a true trapping dead end would make the asymmetric chase unfair and unplayable.

### 7. Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is large, driven by a detailed lobby plus a full 1v4 chase map with many themed route sectors. Theme is whimsical dark fantasy: cozy magical town warmth against ominous ruins, luminous caverns, snow, fog, and pixel-inspired fantasy detail. Use `P4` for the separate lobby and match maps, `P3` for linked exterior and interior traversal, `P6` for the guaranteed looping chase topology, `tiered` for elevation without overhangs, and `CHECK` for the glowing water and cave-volume presentation.
